_meta.what: The privatization map: which basic urban services a citizen depends on are run by PRIVATE FIRMS or PPP concessionaires — not the elected corporation, not a state board. Per city -> per service -> {provider, parent_owner, type, how_became_private, year, controls, approx_people_dependent, regulator, accountability_note, verify, source}. Companion to service_providers.json (which classifies all providers); this file drills into the private/PPP carve-outs only.
_meta.thesis: The atlas's 'unelected city' has a sharper edge than the parastatal one. A water board or development authority is at least state-owned and answerable, however thinly, to the elected government. A PRIVATE monopoly is answerable to shareholders and a sector regulator — the citizen becomes a captive consumer with NO electoral recourse. You cannot vote out Torrent, Adani, CESC or Tata Power.
_meta.conceptual_caveat: Electricity DISTRIBUTION is NOT a 12th-Schedule municipal function (the 12th Schedule covers water, sanitation, roads, planning, public health, etc. — not power). So privatized electricity is NOT a 'devolution failure' in the strict 74th-Amendment sense. The point is broader: basic daily provisioning is offloaded to private monopolies citizens cannot vote out. Read alongside Cooper (privatization of public goods as counterrevolution against democratic claims on the economy) and Ghosh (the corporation/parastatal offloading costly functions while retaining the rent).

type_legend.private_licensee: A long-standing private distribution licensee, often with a colonial/pre-independence lineage (Calcutta Electric Supply 1899; Ahmedabad Electricity Co. 1915). Never publicly owned at the distribution end.
type_legend.privatized_discom: A formerly public/state discom whose management control was sold to a private party post-Electricity-Act-2003 (e.g. CESU Odisha -> TPCODL, 51% to Tata Power, 2020).
type_legend.private_acquisition: A private distribution business bought by another private group (e.g. Reliance Infra's Mumbai suburban discom acquired by Adani, 2018).
type_legend.ppp_concession: A concession/O&M contract awarding operation of a public asset to a private firm for a fixed term (Nagpur water O&M to Orange City Water/Veolia; metro DBFOT to L&T; airport lease to Adani).

_meta.status: Authored 2026-06 from company filings, regulator records, and established news. Key figures cited inline in 'source'. verify:true marks a residual uncertainty (usually a fast-moving figure or a recent restructuring).

electricity.how_became_private: Colonial-era private licensee. The Ahmedabad Electricity Company was incorporated in 1915 and was never a publicly-owned distribution utility. Torrent acquired control by buying out the Gujarat government's residual ~28.89% stake in 1997, forming Torrent Power AEC Ltd; merged into Torrent Power Ltd in 2006.
electricity.controls: Generation + entire electricity distribution for the city of Ahmedabad (and Gandhinagar, Surat, Dahej/Dholera). Torrent Power serves ~4.2 million customers across all its licence areas; the Ahmedabad metro licence area is the core of that base.
electricity.approx_people_dependent: Ahmedabad city ~6.0-7.5 million residents, all on Torrent distribution (no alternative supplier in the licence area).
electricity.regulator: Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) — sets tariffs and licence terms.
electricity.accountability_note: No electoral recourse. The AMC (elected) runs water, roads, waste; power is a private monopoly answerable to GERC and to Torrent's shareholders. A consumer dissatisfied with tariff or reliability can petition GERC but cannot vote the operator out — a structural, not occasional, democratic gap.
electricity.source: Torrent Group history (Wikipedia; Torrent Power 'About Us'); BEE Annual Energy Audit Report, Torrent Power Ltd Ahmedabad FY20-21; Torrent Power ~4.2M customer figure (company).

airport.provider: Ahmedabad International Airport Ltd (Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Intl, SVPI)
airport.parent_owner: Adani Airports Holdings Ltd (Adani Enterprises / Adani Group)
airport.how_became_private: AAI concession (lease) signed 14 Feb 2020; Adani took over operations 7 Nov 2020 under a 50-year lease. Won in the 2019 AAI privatization round in which Adani took six airports.
airport.controls: Operation, management and development of Ahmedabad's only commercial airport; AAI retains only customs/immigration/quarantine/security.
airport.approx_people_dependent: Sole air gateway for the Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar metro region (~8M+); ~11-12M annual passengers pre-disruption.
airport.regulator: AERA (Airports Economic Regulatory Authority) for aeronautical tariffs; MoCA/AAI for the concession.
airport.accountability_note: A 50-year private lease on critical public infrastructure. Part of the Adani urban-infrastructure concentration (see _adani_concentration).
airport.source: BusinessToday/The Week, Nov 2020; Adani SVPIA 'About Us'; AAI concession agreement 14-Feb-2020.

electricity_suburbs_adani.provider: Adani Electricity Mumbai Ltd (AEML) — suburban Mumbai
electricity_suburbs_adani.parent_owner: Adani Group (originally under Adani Transmission Ltd, now Adani Energy Solutions Ltd)
electricity_suburbs_adani.how_became_private: The Mumbai suburban distribution business has been private for decades (BSES, then Reliance Infrastructure). In Aug 2018 Adani acquired Reliance Infrastructure's integrated Mumbai power business — generation (Dahanu), transmission and the suburban retail discom — for ~Rs 18,800 crore, housed in the new AEML.
electricity_suburbs_adani.year: 2018 (Adani acquisition); private lineage via BSES/Reliance from the 20th century
electricity_suburbs_adani.controls: Retail electricity distribution across ~400 sq km of suburban Mumbai; serves over 3 million customers (~12 million people).
electricity_suburbs_adani.approx_people_dependent: ~10-12 million (Adani's stated 3M+ customers x household size, covering most of the suburbs).
electricity_suburbs_adani.accountability_note: Mumbai's power supply is split among BEST (an elected-BMC undertaking, island city), Tata Power and Adani (suburbs). The largest single private supplier, Adani, reaches ~12M people with no electoral accountability — a private monopoly in its licence pockets, regulated only by MERC.
electricity_suburbs_adani.source: Business Today / Business Standard, 29 Aug 2018 (Rs 18,800 cr deal completion); Adani Energy Solutions media release ('3 million customers, 400 sq km'); MERC.

electricity_tata.provider: Tata Power Company Ltd — Mumbai distribution licence
electricity_tata.how_became_private: Tata's Mumbai electricity presence dates to the Tata hydro/Trombay generation lineage (early 20th century); retail distribution licence in Mumbai operates in parallel/overlap with Adani's area, with consumer changeover permitted.
electricity_tata.year: Early 20th-century generation lineage; modern retail distribution licence post-2003
electricity_tata.controls: Retail electricity distribution to 800,000+ consumers (~3-4 million people) in its Mumbai licence area, overlapping Adani's suburban area (parallel licensing).
electricity_tata.accountability_note: Second private supplier in Mumbai; same democratic-deficit logic as Adani — regulated, not elected.
electricity_tata.source: Tata Power 'Mumbai Distribution' (8 lakh+ consumers); Tata Power regulatory pages; MERC.

airport.provider: Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL, CSMIA) + Navi Mumbai International Airport Ltd (NMIAL)
airport.parent_owner: Adani Airports Holdings Ltd (Adani Group); AAHL holds ~74% of MIAL (AAI holds the rest); MIAL holds ~74% of NMIAL (CIDCO 26%)
airport.how_became_private: Adani took over CSMIA operations Feb 2021 from the GVK group (acquiring GVK's stake plus from minority partners). NMIA built as a PPP under MIAL/Adani; inaugurated 25 Dec 2025.
airport.controls: Both of Mumbai's commercial airports — the entire air gateway of the financial capital — now under Adani control.
airport.approx_people_dependent: CSMIA handled ~50M+ passengers/yr; with NMIA, the whole Mumbai air market (tens of millions) is Adani-operated.
airport.accountability_note: Both Mumbai airports under one private group — a striking concentration. See _adani_concentration.
airport.source: CSMIA-Mumbai Adani 'About Us'; Wikipedia CSMIA; travelradar NMIA inauguration 25-Dec-2025; AAHL stake structure (73-74% MIAL, 74% NMIAL).

electricity.parent_owner: RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group (RPSG), formed 2011; CESC is its flagship
electricity.how_became_private: Colonial private licensee. Founded 1899 as the Calcutta Electric Supply Corporation — private from inception, never a state discom. Came under the RPG / later RP-Sanjiv Goenka group; CESC joined the newly-formed RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group on 13 Jul 2011.
electricity.controls: Sole electricity distributor across 567 sq km of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation area plus parts of Howrah, Hooghly and North/South 24 Parganas. CESC group serves ~4.7 million customers.
electricity.approx_people_dependent: The entire KMC population (~4.5M city; ~14M+ metro with surrounding areas) within the 567 sq km licence — a textbook private monopoly.
electricity.accountability_note: A 125-year-old private monopoly. Like Torrent in Ahmedabad, the KMC (elected) runs water/roads/waste while power is a private licensee answerable only to WBERC and RPSG shareholders. No electoral recourse.
electricity.source: CESC Limited (Wikipedia; RPSG 'CESC' page); 567 sq km KMC licence area; ~4.7M customers; RPSG group formed 13-Jul-2011.

metro.provider: L&T Metro Rail (Hyderabad) Ltd (L&TMRHL) — Phase I, 69 km
metro.parent_owner: Larsen & Toubro (L&T) — UNTIL April 2026; now Government of Telangana
metro.how_became_private: Built as a DBFOT PPP — the world's largest metro PPP — L&T SPV; commercial operations from Nov 2017. Concession structured as ~35-year operation + potential extension.
metro.controls: Phase I, 3 corridors, 69 km; ~500,000 (5 lakh) riders/day, record 5.63 lakh (Aug 2024).
metro.regulator: Concession agreement with HMRL (state); no economic regulator equivalent to a SERC.
metro.accountability_note: IMPORTANT UPDATE / STATUS CHANGE: As of April 2026 the Telangana government completed acquisition of Phase I from L&T (~Rs 1,461 crore), bringing the metro fully under government control. So Hyderabad metro is NO LONGER a private/PPP service as of our current date — it is now state-owned. We retain the entry as a historical PPP example (and a rare case of RE-municipalization/de-privatization of a major urban asset). service_providers.json should be updated from type:private to spv/state.
metro.source: Wikipedia Hyderabad Metro; L&T IDPL; Deccan Chronicle / Prokerala (Telangana takes over Phase I from L&T for ~Rs 1,461 cr, share transfer completed April 2026).

electricity.how_became_private: The state discom CESU (Central Electricity Supply Utility of Odisha) was privatized: Tata Power acquired a 51% controlling stake and a 25-year distribution licence via the OERC vesting order of 26 May 2020; management handed over June 2020.
electricity.controls: Electricity distribution across central Odisha incl. Bhubaneswar; ~30.75 lakh (3.08M) customers over 29,354 sq km, serving a population of ~1.36 crore (13.6M).
electricity.approx_people_dependent: ~13.6 million across the licence area; Bhubaneswar (~1M city) is the principal urban node.
electricity.accountability_note: A formerly public discom now under private management control. Classic Electricity-Act-2003-era privatization; consumer recourse is OERC, not the ballot.
electricity.source: Wikipedia TPCODL; Mercom India (Tata Power 51% stake); CSEP discussion note; TPCODL figures (30.75 lakh customers, 1.36 cr population, OERC vesting order 26-May-2020).

water.parent_owner: 50:50 JV — Vishvaraj Environment/Infrastructure (Arun Lakhani) + Veolia Water (France)
water.how_became_private: Nagpur became the first Indian city of its size to outsource its entire water supply to a private operator under a 25-year PPP O&M concession with the Nagpur Municipal Corporation (under JNNURM, later AMRUT). OCW runs production, treatment, transport, storage and last-mile delivery.
water.controls: O&M of the whole urban water cycle: 5 treatment plants (~675 MLD), ~2,100 km network, billing and delivery to ~2.5M+ residents incl. slums.
water.regulator: Concession agreement with NMC (no independent water regulator); MERC has no remit here.
water.accountability_note: Water IS a 12th-Schedule municipal function — so this is the sharpest case: a core municipal service (not electricity) handed to a private O&M operator. The elected NMC retains formal ownership but a private firm runs the tap. Contested locally (NRW disputes, tariff/coverage criticism).
water.source: Veolia India municipal concession contracts; OCW India 'About Us'; Vishvaraj Infrastructure; SANDRP (Nagpur 24x7 critique); 25-year PPP, 675 MLD, ~2,100 km, 50:50 Vishvaraj-Veolia.

sez_datacentre.provider: Atchutapuram/Rambilli SEZ + AdaniConneX Vizag data centre (Google-Adani AI hub)
sez_datacentre.parent_owner: Adani Group (AdaniConneX is a 50:50 Adani-EdgeConneX JV); land via APIIC; Google partnership announced
sez_datacentre.how_became_private: Not a municipal service per se — flagged as private-infrastructure concentration. SEZ/data-centre land sits with APIIC, OUTSIDE the GVMC (elected corporation) entirely. AdaniConneX is building a large data-centre campus; Adani-Google announced a ~USD 15bn AI hub (2026-2030) with gigawatt-scale data centres and captive green energy.
sez_datacentre.controls: Large tracts of coastal land + power + digital infrastructure outside the elected city's jurisdiction.
sez_datacentre.approx_people_dependent: n/a (not a household service) — significance is land/power/employment concentration and the bypassing of the elected GVMC.
sez_datacentre.regulator: APIIC / state industries dept; no municipal oversight.
sez_datacentre.accountability_note: Illustrates the pattern beyond household services: the highest-value urban land and infrastructure is assembled by the state for a private conglomerate, outside the elected corporation. See _adani_concentration.
sez_datacentre.source: Adani/Google media release (India's largest data-centre campus, Visakhapatnam, ~USD 15bn 2026-2030); DCD/EdgeConneX (300 MW AdaniConneX park); APIIC land; service_providers.json visakhapatnam _note.

_adani_concentration.what: A standalone concentration-of-private-power risk that cuts across cities. One conglomerate now sits astride multiple categories of urban infrastructure across our atlas.
_adani_concentration.electricity: Adani Electricity Mumbai (AEML): ~3M customers / ~10-12M people in suburban Mumbai (acquired from Reliance Infra, 2018, Rs 18,800 cr).
_adani_concentration.airports: Adani Airports Holdings (AAHL) is India's LARGEST private airport operator — 8 airports, ~25% of national passenger footfall and ~33% of air cargo. Directly relevant to our cities: BOTH Mumbai airports (CSMIA, from GVK in 2021; Navi Mumbai, opened Dec 2025) and Ahmedabad (SVPI, 50-yr lease from 2020).
_adani_concentration.ports: Adani Ports & SEZ (APSEZ) is India's largest port operator — ~27% all-India cargo market share (FY26), ~500 MMT throughput, eyeing 1 billion tonnes by 2030.
_adani_concentration.data_centres_and_land: AdaniConneX (Adani-EdgeConneX JV) building India's largest data-centre campus at Visakhapatnam with Google (~USD 15bn 2026-2030); SEZ land via APIIC, outside the elected GVMC.
_adani_concentration.risk_framing: Across electricity, airports, ports, data centres and SEZ land, a single private group controls or is building chokepoints of urban life in multiple atlas cities — none of it subject to municipal election. This is the 'unelected city' at its most concentrated: not merely many small carve-outs, but one conglomerate accumulating across the whole infrastructural stack, regulated piecemeal (MERC, AERA, OERC, state industry depts) and accountable to no electorate.
_adani_concentration.source: Adani Energy Solutions; AAHL (8 airports, 25% pax, 33% cargo); APSEZ (Wikipedia, ITLN, ~27.1% cargo share FY26); Adani/Google Visakhapatnam release.

_headline_numbers.cities_with_privatized_electricity: 4 of 6 majors have privatized/private electricity distribution at the city level: Ahmedabad (Torrent), Mumbai-suburbs (Adani + Tata), Kolkata (CESC). Plus Bhubaneswar (TPCODL). Chennai (TANGEDCO), Bengaluru (BESCOM), Hyderabad (TGSPDCL), Visakhapatnam (APEPDCL) remain STATE discoms.
_headline_numbers.dominant_private_players: Adani Group (electricity Mumbai + airports Mumbai/Ahmedabad + ports + data centres), Torrent Group (Ahmedabad electricity), Tata Power (Mumbai electricity + TPCODL Odisha), RP-Sanjiv Goenka/CESC (Kolkata electricity), Veolia/Vishvaraj (Nagpur water), L&T (Hyderabad metro — now de-privatized 2026).
_headline_numbers.approx_population_on_private_electricity: Torrent (Ahmedabad city) ~6-7.5M + Adani+Tata (Mumbai suburbs) ~12-15M + CESC (Kolkata licence area) ~4.5M+ + TPCODL (central Odisha incl. Bhubaneswar) ~13.6M ≈ ON THE ORDER OF 35-40 MILLION people on privately-distributed electricity across these cities/regions (the discom figures span licence areas wider than the core city).
_headline_numbers.caveat: Electricity is NOT a 12th-Schedule municipal function, so its privatization is not a devolution failure per se. The genuinely municipal privatization in this map is NAGPUR WATER (a 12th-Schedule function under private O&M). The deeper point is the democratic deficit: tens of millions depend daily on private monopolies they cannot vote out.
